# GitHub Repository Context Generator

Generate AI-ready PDF documentation from your GitHub repositories. Designed to help LLMs (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Cursor, Copilot, etc.) understand your codebase instantly.

## Features

- **GitHub API Integration** - Authenticate with your Personal Access Token to fetch repositories
- **Smart Repository Selection** - Search, filter by language/visibility, sort by various criteria
- **Professional PDF Generation** - Cover page, table of contents, executive summary, bookmarks
- **Markdown Rendering** - Headings, lists, tables, code blocks with syntax highlighting, blockquotes
- **AI Metadata Inference** - Framework, libraries, architecture, database, CI/CD detection from project files
- **Language Breakdown** - Pie charts and detailed language distribution for each repository
- **Multiple Export Formats** - PDF, Markdown, and JSON downloads
- **Pagination Support** - Automatically fetches all repositories via GitHub API pagination
- **Error Handling** - Graceful handling of rate limits, timeouts, missing READMEs
- **Security** - Tokens processed in-memory only, never stored or logged

## Screenshots

| Component | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| **Input** | GitHub username + token with show/hide toggle |
| **Validation** | Token verification with welcome message |
| **Repository List** | Searchable, filterable, sortable table with checkboxes |
| **PDF Cover** | Professional cover with stats summary |
| **Repo Section** | Metadata, languages chart, rendered README, AI metadata |

## Architecture

```
streamlit_app.py     # Main application (single-file)
├── GitHubClient     # GitHub REST API wrapper with pagination
├── MarkdownRenderer # markdown-it-py to ReportLab flowable converter
├── MetadataInferrer # Framework/library detection from project files
├── PDFGenerator     # ReportLab document builder with TOC
├── CodeBlock        # Custom flowable for syntax-highlighted code
└── DocWithTOC       # BaseDocTemplate with TOC and page templates
```

## Installation

### Prerequisites

- Python 3.12+
- Git
- GitHub Personal Access Token

### Local Setup

```bash
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/yourusername/github-repo-context-generator.git
cd github-repo-context-generator

# Create virtual environment
python -m venv venv

# Activate it
# Windows:
venv\Scripts\activate
# macOS/Linux:
source venv/bin/activate

# Install dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Run the application
streamlit run streamlit_app.py
```

### Deploy on Streamlit Community Cloud

1. Push the repository to GitHub
2. Go to [share.streamlit.io](https://share.streamlit.io)
3. Deploy the app (no additional configuration required)
4. Main file: `streamlit_app.py`

## GitHub Personal Access Token

### Creating a Token

1. Go to **GitHub Settings > Developer settings > Personal access tokens > Fine-grained tokens** (or **Tokens (classic)**)
2. Click **Generate new token**
3. For **Fine-grained tokens**: Set repository access to **All repositories** or **Select repositories**
4. Under **Permissions > Repository permissions**, set **Contents: Read**, **Metadata: Read**
5. For **Tokens (classic)**: Enable scopes `repo` (for private repos) and `read:user`
6. Copy the token and paste into the application

### Required Scopes

| Scope | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `repo` | Access private repositories |
| `read:user` | Read user profile data |
| `read:org` | (Optional) Read organization repos |

## Usage

1. Enter your GitHub username
2. Enter your Personal Access Token
3. Click **Validate**
4. Select repositories using checkboxes
5. Use search, filters, and sort options to find specific repositories
6. Click **Generate PDF**
7. Download the PDF (and optionally Markdown/JSON)

## Output

The generated PDF includes:

- **Cover Page** - Title, timestamp, user info, repository count, aggregated stats
- **Executive Summary** - Total stars, forks, language distribution, pie chart
- **Table of Contents** - Clickable links to each repository section
- **Repository Sections** (one per selected repo):
  - Full metadata table
  - Language breakdown with colored bars
  - Rendered README content
  - AI-Inferred Metadata section

### AI Metadata Detection

The system analyzes project files to infer:

| Field | Detection Method |
|-------|-----------------|
| Framework | `package.json` dependencies, `requirements.txt`, config files |
| Build Tool | `vite.config.*`, `webpack.config.js`, `Makefile`, `CMakeLists.txt` |
| Package Manager | `package-lock.json`, `yarn.lock`, `Cargo.toml`, `go.mod`, `pyproject.toml` |
| Database | ORM dependencies (`prisma`, `sqlalchemy`, `mongoose`) |
| CI/CD | `.github/workflows`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `Jenkinsfile` |
| Containerization | `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.yml` |
| Architecture | Framework-specific patterns |

## Troubleshooting

| Issue | Solution |
|-------|----------|
| **Invalid token** | Verify token scopes include `repo` and `read:user` |
| **Rate limited** | Wait for the reset time shown in the error message |
| **No repositories found** | Check token has access to the repositories |
| **PDF generation fails** | Ensure selected repos have at least a README or basic content |
| **Timeout** | Try selecting fewer repositories |

## FAQ

**Q: Are tokens stored anywhere?**
A: No. Tokens are held in memory only and cleared after each session.

**Q: Does this clone repositories?**
A: No. Only GitHub REST API calls are made. No cloning, no Git history.

**Q: Can I use this with private repositories?**
A: Yes, if your token has the `repo` scope and access to the repositories.

**Q: How many repositories can I process at once?**
A: There's no hard limit, but processing many repositories will take longer.

**Q: Are AI APIs used for metadata inference?**
A: No. Metadata is inferred purely from file analysis and repository metadata.

## Future Improvements

- Batch processing with background workers
- Repository dependency graph
- Code complexity analysis
- Multi-language README rendering
- Git commit statistics

🧠 Memory System (`memory/memory_engine.py`) ### Three-Layer Memory | Layer | Storage | Content | |---|---|---| | **Short-term** | `data/short_term_memory.json` | Conversation turns (role + content + timestamp) | | **Long-term** | ChromaDB (`chroma_db/`) | Semantically embedded knowledge chunks | | **Profile** | `data/user_profiles.json` | Structured facts: name, email, location, skills, goals, education, occupation, projects, facts | ### Auto-Extraction Every user message is scanned with regex patterns to automatically populate the profile: - **Name**: `"my name is ..."` → `profile.name` - **Location**: `"I'm from Surat"` → `profile.location` - **Skills**: `"I know Python, React"` → `profile.skills[]` - **Goals**: `"I want to find an ML internship"` → `profile.goals[]` - **Occupation**: `"I am an AIML student"` → `profile.occupation` - **Education**: `"pursuing B.Tech Computer Science"` → `profile.education[]` ### Context Budget To avoid LLM token overflow, context is capped before every LLM call: - Live search results: ≤ 4,000 chars - Memory/profile context: ≤ 2,000 chars - Web search timeout: 12 seconds max --- ## 🔍 Web Search (`tools/web_search.py`) All search is **real-time**, requires **no API keys**, and runs automatically. ### Smart Router (`smart_research()`) Detects query type and routes to the right source: ``` Job query → job_search() → Internshala scraper + direct links Paper query → arxiv_search() → arXiv API (live 2026 data) + semantic_scholar_search() General → duckduckgo_search() → DuckDuckGo with retry/backoff ``` ### Auto-Trigger Keywords The `/chat` endpoint auto-triggers live search when the message contains: `internship, job, hiring, find, search, list, latest, recent, 2024, 2025, 2026, papers, research, news, trending, salary, vacancy, in surat, in india, ...` ### Sources | Source | What It Provides | API Key | |---|---|---| | arXiv API | Live papers in cs.AI, cs.LG, cs.CL, cs.CV, etc. | None | | Semantic Scholar | Paper metadata, abstracts, DOI/arXiv links | None | | Internshala | Real job/internship listings by city & domain | None | | DuckDuckGo | General web results (3-attempt backoff) | None | --- ## OAuth flows handled at: ``` GET /api/v1/integrations/google/auth GET /api/v1/integrations/google/callback GET /api/v1/integrations/linkedin/auth GET /api/v1/integrations/linkedin/callback ``` --- ## 🎤 Voice (`assistants/voice.py`) | Feature | Engine | Fallback | |---|---|---| | Speech-to-Text | Google STT via `SpeechRecognition` | Informative error message | | Text-to-Speech | gTTS (Google TTS) | Informative error message | ```http POST /api/v1/voice/stt # { "audio_base64": "...", "mime_type": "audio/wav" } POST /api/v1/voice/tts # { "text": "Hello world" } ``` --- ## ⏰ Workflows (`workflows/scheduler.py`) APScheduler-powered background job system, started automatically on app launch. ```http POST /api/v1/workflows/cron # Add cron job (expression + workflow_type) POST /api/v1/workflows/interval # Add interval job (hours + minutes) GET /api/v1/workflows # List all jobs for current user DELETE /api/v1/workflows/{id} # Remove a job ``` --- ## 📡 API Referen

# StackOverflow Clone A full-stack social Q&A platform inspired by StackOverflow, built with **Express 5 + MongoDB** and **Next.js 15 + React 19**. Features multi-language support (6 languages), Telegram-assisted OTP delivery, social feed with friend system, Q&A with voting, subscription plans via Razorpay, and device-aware login security. ![Frontend Screenshot](stack/public/frontend.png) --- ## Features - **Multi-Language Support** — 6 languages (English, Spanish, Hindi, Portuguese, Chinese, French) with i18next. Language switch requires OTP verification via email (French) or phone (all others via Telegram to admin). - **Device-Aware Login** — Chrome desktop triggers OTP before granting access; mobile login restricted to UTC 10:00–13:00. All logins recorded in history. - **OTP Infrastructure** — Dual-layer: login OTP via email (Resend); language-switch OTP via email or Telegram; forgot-password OTP via Telegram + in-memory store. - **Social Feed** — Create posts with image/video upload, like, comment, share with friends. - **Q&A System** — Ask questions, post answers, upvote/downvote, tag-based discovery. - **Friend System** — Send, accept, decline, remove friend requests; friend-based posting limits. - **Subscription Plans** — Razorpay-powered plans (Free/Bronze/Silver/Gold) controlling daily question posting limits. - **Rate Limiting** — Auth routes 30 requests/15min, OTP 5 requests/min per IP. # Portfolio Website

A modern personal portfolio built with Next.js (App Router), TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and reusable UI components.

## Tech Stack

- Next.js 14
- React 18
- TypeScript
- Tailwind CSS
- Radix UI primitives
- Framer Motion

## Project Structure

- `app/` - App Router pages, layout, global styles, API routes
- `components/` - Reusable page and UI components
- `data/` - Static JSON data (career timeline)
- `lib/` - Shared constants, content, and utilities
- `public/` - Static assets
- `styles/` - Additional global styling

## Getting Started

### 1) Install dependencies

Using npm:

```bash
npm install
```

Using pnpm:

```bash
pnpm install
```

### 2) Run development server

Using npm:

```bash
npm run dev
```

Using pnpm:

```bash
pnpm dev
```

Open http://localhost:3000 in your browser.

## Available Scripts

- `dev` - Start development server
- `build` - Build for production
- `start` - Start production server
- `lint` - Run lint checks

## API Endpoints

- `POST /api/contact` - Contact form handler
- `GET /api/career` - Career data endpoint

## Deployment

This project can be deployed on Vercel or any Node.js hosting platform that supports Next.js.

Production build:

```bash
npm run build
npm run start
```

## Notes

- Keep portfolio text/content in `lib/constants` and `lib/content` for easier updates.
- Static media should be placed under `public/`.

# FinStream: AI-Powered Financial Sentiment Intelligence

![FinStream project overview](project.png)

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-3.11%2B-3776AB?logo=python&logoColor=white)
![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-Backend-009688?logo=fastapi&logoColor=white)

![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Add%20Your%20Choice-lightgrey)

FinStream is a full-stack AIML project for real-time financial news sentiment analysis. It combines a production-grade FastAPI inference backend, a modern Flask frontend dashboard, and a complete offline evaluation pipeline for model performance tracking.

## Project Overview

### What FinStream solves
- Ingests financial news text from users.
- Runs transformer-based sentiment inference using Hugging Face.
- Returns actionable sentiment classes with confidence scores.
- Visualizes predictions in an interactive, portfolio-ready UI.

### Current model
- Hugging Face model: [hitenvk22/FinStream-Sentiment](https://huggingface.co/hitenvk22/finstream-sentiment)

### Live Links
- Backend: [https://finstream-zypg.onrender.com](https://finstream-zypg.onrender.com)
- Frontend: [https://frontend-xsuz.onrender.com](https://frontend-xsuz.onrender.com)
- HF Space (GPU API): [https://hitenvk22-finstream-api.hf.space](https://hitenvk22-finstream-api.hf.space)

Deployment is in progress. The frontend talks to the backend through the Render service connection and the configured environment variables.

### Model Evaluation Snapshot

![FinStream classification report screenshot](docs/screenshots/model_classification_metrics.png)

This snapshot captures a notebook test-set result with 83.36% accuracy and a full classification report for bullish, neutral, and bearish labels.

### Training History Snapshot

![FinStream training history graph](docs/screenshots/model_convergence_graph.png)

This plot shows training loss trending downward, validation loss stabilizing, and validation F1 / precision / recall converging across epochs.


## Architecture Diagram

		R --> F
		F --> U

		E[Evaluation Script + Notebook] --> M
		E --> P[(evaluation/plots)]
		E --> S[(evaluation/results)]
```

## Features

- Modern responsive frontend with dark mode and animations.
- Real-time prediction requests with `fetch()`.
- Sentiment output with confidence score and color-coded cards.
- FastAPI backend with startup model loading and CORS support.
- Health check endpoint for uptime monitoring.
- Structured exception handling and logging.
- GPU-aware inference (CUDA if available, CPU fallback).
- Full evaluation suite with metrics and visual diagnostics.
- Render-ready deployment setup using Procfile-based launch commands.

## Tech Stack

- Backend: FastAPI, Uvicorn, Transformers, PyTorch, Pydantic
- Frontend: Flask, Bootstrap 5, Chart.js, custom CSS/JS
- Evaluation: scikit-learn, pandas, matplotlib, seaborn
- Platform: Render
- Tooling: VS Code, Jupyter Notebook

## Screenshots

The screenshots below are taken from the current FinStream UI and show both the single-text prediction flow and the final portfolio-style dashboard.

### Single Text Prediction

![FinStream single-text prediction dashboard](docs/screenshots/single_text_predcition.png)

![FinStream CSV batch analysis dashboard](docs/screenshots/csv_prediction.png)

This view is used for CSV upload testing, batch sentiment processing, report ID generation, and PDF report download. It demonstrates the batch workflow for message-wise sentiment analysis and sentiment net summary reporting.



## Model Training Details

- Model family: Transformer-based sequence classification.
- Finetuned checkpoint: `hitenvk22/FinStream-Sentiment`.
- Hugging Face model page: [https://huggingface.co/hitenvk22/finstream-sentiment](https://huggingface.co/hitenvk22/finstream-sentiment)

## Hugging Face Integration

repo.readme:
# TickerFlow

A fully Dockerized financial data pipeline that decouples external API fetching from data serving. Built with FastAPI, Celery, Redis, PostgreSQL, and Apache Airflow.

## Architecture

The system follows a layered architecture where the web server never directly calls external APIs. It reads preprocessed data from PostgreSQL and triggers background tasks when data is stale or missing. Workers handle all external requests with automatic retry logic.

![Full Architecture](docs/Full_architecture.png)

```
Client ──▶ FastAPI (api/) ──▶ PostgreSQL ◀── Celery Worker (workers/)
                │                              │
                │  triggers task               │  fetches data
                ▼                              ▼
            Redis (broker)              External APIs
```

Key design principles:

- **Decoupling**: API server and data fetching run in separate processes. The API stays fast and responsive regardless of external API latency.
- **Resilience**: Celery retries failed fetches with exponential backoff (up to 3 retries). Airflow DAGs have 2 retries with 2-minute delays.
- **Separation of concerns**: Real-time data fetching (Celery) and scheduled batch ETL (Airflow) operate independently.

## Infrastructure

All services run in Docker containers, orchestrated via Docker Compose. The stack consists of 6 containers:

![Docker Containers](docs/Ticker_flow_DockerOPS.png)

| Service | Role | Port |
|---------|------|------|
| API | FastAPI + Uvicorn | 8000 |
| Worker | Celery task processor | -- |
| Postgres | Database | 5432 |
| Redis | Celery broker | 6379 |
| Airflow Webserver | DAG management UI | 8080 |
| Airflow Scheduler | DAG execution engine | -- |

### Container Dependencies

- API depends on Postgres (healthy) and Redis (healthy)
- Worker depends on Postgres (healthy) and Redis (healthy)
- Airflow services depend on `airflow-init` completing successfully
- `airflow-init` runs database migrations and creates the admin user, then exits

### Startup

**First-time start (build images and boot stack):**

```bash
docker compose up --build
```

The API server becomes available at `http://localhost:8000`. Airflow web UI is at `http://localhost:8080` (login: admin / admin).

![API Server Running](docs/backend_api_running.png)

**Rebuild after code changes:**

```bash
docker compose up -d --build
```

This rebuilds API, worker, and airflow images in parallel, then restarts only containers with changes. No data loss.

**Stop the stack:**

```bash
docker compose down
```

**Stop and wipe all data (Postgres volume included):**

```bash
docker compose down -v
```

## API Endpoints

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| GET | `/` | Root API info with endpoint listing |
| GET | `/health` | Database connectivity check |
| GET | `/stocks/{symbol}` | Latest stock price |
| GET | `/stocks/history/{symbol}` | Historical daily prices (default 100, configurable via `?limit=`) |
| GET | `/stocks/history/{symbol}/export` | Download stock history as CSV |
| GET | `/news/{symbol}` | Latest news articles (default 20) |
| GET | `/news/{symbol}/export` | Download news articles as CSV |
| GET | `/symbols` | List all available stock symbols with data |

If data does not exist for a requested symbol, the API returns `202 Accepted` and triggers a background Celery task to fetch it. Retry the request after 10-15 seconds.

Interactive API documentation is available at `/docs` (Swagger UI).

![Swagger UI](docs/swagger.png)

## ETL Pipeline

Apache Airflow runs scheduled ETL DAGs for each tracked symbol (AAPL, MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, TSLA). Each DAG runs every 30 minutes and follows a three-phase pipeline:

![ETL Pipeline DAG](docs/ETL_pipeline.png)

### Phase 1: Extract

Fetches raw data from external APIs:

- **Stock price**: Alpha Vantage `GLOBAL_QUOTE` endpoint
- **Stock history**: Alpha Vantage `TIME_SERIES_DAILY` endpoint
- **News**: NewsAPI `/v2/everything` endpoint

Each extraction returns metadata including success/failure status, source, timestamp, and raw response.

### Phase 2: Transform

Validates and cleans the extracted data:

- Stock price: Validates price is positive, parses change percentage, converts volume to integer
- Stock history: Validates OHLC values (no negatives, high >= low), parses dates, drops invalid records
- News: Filters articles without URLs, truncates title/summary to field limits, normalizes timestamps

Each transformation returns metrics: received, passed, failed, skipped.

### Phase 3: Load

Writes cleaned data to PostgreSQL:

- Stock price: Direct insert with timestamp
- Stock history: Bulk upsert using `ON CONFLICT (symbol, date) DO UPDATE`
- News: Insert with `ON CONFLICT (url) DO NOTHING` for deduplication

Each load returns metrics: inserted, updated, failed.

![ETL Pipeline Logs](docs/ETL_pipeline_logs.png)

### DAG Structure

Each symbol gets its own DAG (`tickerflow_etl_aapl`, `tickerflow_etl_msft`, etc.) with 9 tasks in a linear pipeline:

```
extract ──▶ transform ──▶ load
extract_history ──▶ transform_history ──▶ load_history
extract_news ──▶ transform_news ──▶ load_news
```

All three branches run in parallel within each DAG execution.

## Celery Workers

Celery handles real-time, API-triggered data fetching:

| Task | Trigger | Behavior |
|------|---------|----------|
| `fetch_stock_price` | API cache miss | Fetches from Alpha Vantage, upserts into `stocks` table |
| `fetch_stock_history` | API cache miss | Fetches daily series, deduplicates by `(symbol, date)` |
| `fetch_news` | API cache miss | Fetches from NewsAPI, deduplicates by `url` |
| `refresh_all` | Manual/periodic | Iterates all tracked symbols, chains price + history + news |

All tasks use `max_retries=3` with exponential backoff (60s, 120s, 240s).

## Database Schema

Three tables, auto-created by `docker/01-init-schema.sql` on first Postgres startup:

### stocks
| Column | Type | Notes |
|--------|------|-------|
| id | SERIAL | Primary key |
| symbol | VARCHAR(10) | Indexed |
| price | NUMERIC(12,6) | |
| change | NUMERIC(12,6) | |
| change_pct | NUMERIC(10,6) | |
| volume | BIGINT | |
| timestamp | TIMESTAMPTZ | UTC |
| created_at | TIMESTAMPTZ | Auto-generated |

### stock_history (partitioned by month)

The table uses PostgreSQL native range partitioning on `date` to improve query performance and enable partition pruning for time-range queries.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|--------|------|-------|
| symbol | VARCHAR(10) | Composite PK with date |
| date | DATE | Composite PK with symbol, partition key |
| open | NUMERIC(12,6) | |
| high | NUMERIC(12,6) | |
| low | NUMERIC(12,6) | |
| close | NUMERIC(12,6) | |
| volume | BIGINT | |
| created_at | TIMESTAMPTZ | Auto-generated |

Monthly partitions are pre-created for 2025 Q4 through 2026 (16 partitions total). Data outside these ranges goes into a default partition. Partition pruning happens automatically on date-filtered queries.

**Existing data migration** (only if you already ran the old schema):

```bash
docker compose cp docker/03-migrate-partitions.sql postgres:/tmp/
docker compose exec postgres psql -U tickerflow -d tickerflow -f /tmp/03-migrate-partitions.sql
```

### news
| Column | Type | Notes |
|--------|------|-------|
| id | SERIAL | Primary key |
| symbol | VARCHAR(10) | Indexed |
| title | TEXT | |
| source | VARCHAR(255) | |
| url | TEXT | UNIQUE |
| published_at | TIMESTAMPTZ | |
| summary | TEXT | |
| created_at | TIMESTAMPTZ | Auto-generated |

## Environment Variables

| Variable | Required | Default |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `DATABASE_URL` | Yes | `postgresql://tickerflow:tickerflow@postgres:5432/tickerflow` |
| `REDIS_URL` | Yes | `redis://redis:6379/0` |
| `ALPHA_VANTAGE_API_KEY` | Yes | -- |
| `NEWS_API_KEY` | Yes | -- |

## Project Structure

```
├── api/               FastAPI web server
│   ├── main.py        App creation, CORS, router inclusion
│   ├── database.py    SQLAlchemy engine, session, get_db dependency
│   ├── models.py      ORM: Stock, StockHistory, News
│   ├── schemas.py     Pydantic response models
│   └── routes.py      Endpoint definitions
├── workers/           Celery background workers
│   ├── celery_app.py  Celery app instance with Redis config
│   ├── fetchers.py    HTTP fetchers for Alpha Vantage and NewsAPI
│   └── tasks.py       Celery task definitions with retry logic
├── airflow/           Airflow ETL pipeline
│   └── dags/
│       ├── tickerflow_etl.py       DAG definition (5 symbols)
│       └── etl_utils/
│           ├── extract.py          API data extraction
│           ├── transform.py        Validation and cleaning
│           └── load.py             PostgreSQL bulk upsert
├── docker/
│   ├── api.Dockerfile
│   ├── worker.Dockerfile
│   ├── airflow.Dockerfile
│   ├── 01-init-schema.sql          Database schema (partitioned)
│   ├── 02-init-airflow.sh          Airflow DB creation
│   └── 03-migrate-partitions.sql   Migration script for existing data
├── docs/
│   └── api_testing.json            Postman collection
├── docker-compose.yml
├── requirements.txt
└── requirements-airflow.txt
```

# AI Healthcare Assistant

Full-stack healthcare platform with:

- User AI consultation web app
- Nearby hospital discovery and directions
- Appointment booking flow
- Hospital-facing dashboard web app
- Node.js + Express + MongoDB backend API

This repository is a multi-app workspace, not a single frontend.

## Project Architecture

### Applications

1. User app (`User`)
- AI symptom conversation (Groq)
- Emergency symptom detection
- Nearby hospitals page
- User authentication and consultation history
- Appointment booking

2. Hospital app (`Hospital`)
- Hospital registration/login
- Manage hospital profile and hospital-side workflows
- Appointment operations via backend APIs

3. Backend API (`Hospital/backend`)
- Auth APIs for users and hospitals
- Hospital registry and nearby search
- Chat session/history APIs
- Appointment APIs for both user and hospital sides

### High-Level Flow

1. User talks to AI in the User app.
2. User can open Nearby Hospitals and search by live location.
3. User books appointment with a selected hospital.
4. Hospital app consumes the same backend to view and update appointments.

## Repository Structure

```text
ai-health-assistant/
	User/                # User-facing React app
	Hospital/            # Hospital-facing React app
		backend/           # Express + MongoDB backend API
	DEPLOYMENT.md        # Render + Vercel deployment steps
	render.yaml          # Render blueprint config
```

## Tech Stack

### Frontend
- React 19 + Vite
- React Router
- React Markdown
- Three.js + @react-three/fiber + @react-three/drei (User app visual layer)

### Backend
- Node.js + Express
- MongoDB + Mongoose
- JWT authentication
- bcryptjs password hashing

### Integrations
- Groq API (AI responses)
- Browser Geolocation
- Google Maps directions (client-side link out)

## Key Features

### User App
- AI-guided symptom assessment conversation
- Emergency cue detection and urgent prompts
- Nearby hospital discovery with distance sorting
- Appointment booking with optional chat context
- Multi-language support (English, Hindi, Gujarati)

### Hospital App
- Hospital onboarding and login
- Hospital data management
- Appointment status handling (pending, confirmed, completed)

### Backend
- User auth: register, login, profile
- Hospital auth: register, login
- Chat session lifecycle and history persistence
- Nearby hospital APIs
- Appointment APIs for both user and hospital roles

## Recent UX Fixes

- Added loading spinner state when user clicks "Find Nearby Hospitals" so long navigation/data preparation is visible.
- Corrected open/closed badge logic so unknown operating status is not incorrectly shown as "Closed".

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 18+
- npm 9+
- MongoDB Atlas (or compatible MongoDB)
- Groq API key

## Local Development Setup

### 1. Clone

```bash
git clone https://github.com/HitenKatariya/ai-health-assistant.git
cd ai-health-assistant
```

### 2. Install Dependencies

```bash
cd User
npm install

cd ../Hospital
npm install

cd backend
npm install
```

### 3. Configure Environment Variables

Create these files:

1. `Hospital/backend/.env`

```env
MONGODB_URI=mongodb+srv://<username>:<password>@<cluster>/<db>?retryWrites=true&w=majority
PORT=3001
NODE_ENV=development
JWT_SECRET=replace_with_a_strong_secret
JWT_EXPIRE=30d
CORS_ORIGIN=http://localhost:5173,http://localhost:5174
```

2. `User/.env`

```env
VITE_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:3001
VITE_GROQ_API_KEY=your_groq_api_key
```

3. `Hospital/.env`

```env
VITE_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:3001
```

Notes:
- Frontends also accept `VITE_API_URL` as fallback.
- Default frontend API fallback is `http://localhost:3001`.

### 4. Run Services (3 terminals)

1. Backend

```bash
cd Hospital/backend
npm run dev
```

2. User app

```bash
cd User
npm run dev -- --port 5173
```

3. Hospital app

```bash
cd Hospital
npm run dev -- --port 5174
```

Open:

- User app: `http://localhost:5173`
- Hospital app: `http://localhost:5174`
- Backend: `http://localhost:3001`

## Scripts

### User (`User/package.json`)
- `npm run dev`
- `npm run build`
- `npm run preview`
- `npm run lint`

### Hospital (`Hospital/package.json`)
- `npm run dev`
- `npm run build`
- `npm run preview`
- `npm run lint`

### Backend (`Hospital/backend/package.json`)
- `npm run dev` (nodemon)
- `npm start`

## API Overview

Base URL: `http://localhost:3001`

### Auth
- `POST /api/auth/register`
- `POST /api/auth/login`
- `GET /api/auth/me`
- `PUT /api/auth/profile`
- `PUT /api/auth/password`
- `DELETE /api/auth/account`

### Hospitals
- `POST /api/hospitals/register`
- `POST /api/hospitals/login`
- `GET /api/hospitals`
- `GET /api/hospitals/:id`
- `POST /api/hospitals/nearby`

### Chat
- `POST /api/chat/sessions`
- `GET /api/chat/sessions`
- `GET /api/chat/sessions/:sessionId`
- `POST /api/chat/sessions/:sessionId/messages`
- `POST /api/chat/sessions/:sessionId/hospitals`
- `PUT /api/chat/sessions/:sessionId/end`

### Appointments
- User routes:
	- `POST /api/appointments`
	- `GET /api/appointments`
	- `GET /api/appointments/:id`
- Hospital routes:
	- `GET /api/appointments/hospital`
	- `PATCH /api/appointments/hospital/:id/status`

## Deployment

Production deployment instructions are documented in `DEPLOYMENT.md`.

Current deployment model:
- Backend on Render
- User frontend on Vercel
- Hospital frontend on Vercel

Live deployment links:
- User app: https://ai-health-assistant-chi.vercel.app
- Hospital app: https://ai-health-assistant-hospital.vercel.app/
- Backend API: https://ai-health-assistant-backend-ejmt.onrender.com

Important production settings:
- Set frontend `VITE_API_BASE_URL` to your Render backend URL.
- Set backend `CORS_ORIGIN` to both Vercel domains (comma-separated).

## Medical Disclaimer

This project is for informational and educational support only. It does not replace professional medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment.

## Troubleshooting

### Nearby hospitals are slow to appear
- Check browser geolocation permission.
- Verify backend connectivity and MongoDB status.
- Confirm frontend `VITE_API_BASE_URL` points to a live backend.

### Hospital shows incorrect closed status
- Ensure hospital `isOpen` data is stored as explicit boolean.
- Unknown status should render without a closed badge.

### CORS errors
- Verify backend `CORS_ORIGIN` includes both frontend origins.
- Restart backend after env changes.

# 🌐 AWS 3-Tier Web Application Architecture using VPC

![Architecture](images/3-tierarchitecture-1.png)

This project demonstrates how to deploy a **secure 3-tier web application architecture on AWS** using a custom **Virtual Private Cloud (VPC)**.

🔒 Secure | ⚙️ Modular | ☁️ AWS-Powered

---

# 🧱 Architecture Diagram

![Architecture](images/architecture-diagram.png)

---

# 🛠 Tech Stack

| Layer | Component | AWS Service |
|------|-----------|-------------|
| Web | Nginx | EC2 (Public Subnet) |
| Application | Apache Tomcat | EC2 (Private Subnet) |
| Database | MySQL | EC2 (Private Subnet) |
| Network | VPC | AWS VPC |

---

# 🌐 Step 1: Create VPC

CIDR Block:

```
10.1.0.0/16
```

![VPC](images/vpc.png)

---

# 🌐 Step 2: Create Subnets

| Subnet | CIDR | Purpose |
|------|------|------|
| Public | 10.1.1.0/24 | Web Server |
| Private | 10.1.2.0/24 | App Server |
| Private | 10.1.3.0/24 | Database |

![Subnet](images/Subnet-creation.png)

---

# 🌐 Step 3: Configure Internet Gateway

Attach Internet Gateway to the VPC.

![Internet Gateway](images/Internet Gateway.png)

---

# 🌐 Step 4: Configure NAT Gateway

Private instances use NAT Gateway to access the internet securely.

![NAT Gateway](images/NAT-gateway.png)

---

# 🌐 Step 5: Configure Route Tables

### Public Route Table

```
0.0.0.0/0 → Internet Gateway
```

![Route Table](images/Route table.png)

### Private Route Table

```
0.0.0.0/0 → NAT Gateway
```

![Private Route Table](images/Private-rt.png)

![Web Route Table](images/web-rt(1).png)

![Web Route Table](images/web-rt(2).png)

---

# 💻 Step 6: Launch EC2 Instances

Three EC2 instances were created:

- Web Server (Nginx)
- App Server (Tomcat)
- Database Server (MySQL)

![Instances](images/Instances.png)

---

# 🌍 Web Tier – Nginx

Install Nginx on the Web EC2 instance.

```bash
sudo apt update
sudo apt install nginx -y
sudo systemctl start nginx
sudo systemctl enable nginx
```

---

# ⚙ Application Tier – Apache Tomcat

Install Java and Apache Tomcat.

```bash
sudo apt update
sudo apt install default-jdk -y
wget https://downloads.apache.org/tomcat/tomcat-11/v11.0.9/bin/apache-tomcat-11.0.9.tar.gz
tar -xvzf apache-tomcat-11.0.9.tar.gz
cd apache-tomcat-11.0.9/bin
./startup.sh
```

![Tomcat](images/Tomcat.png)

---

# 🛢 Database Tier – MySQL

Install MySQL server.

```bash
sudo apt update
sudo apt install mysql-server -y
sudo systemctl start mysql
sudo systemctl enable mysql
```

![MySQL](images/MySQL.png)

---

# 🔐 MySQL Configuration

Edit the MySQL configuration file:

```bash
sudo vim /etc/mysql/mysql.conf.d/mysqld.cnf
```

Default:

```
bind-address = 127.0.0.1
```

![MySQL Bind](images/MySQL bind-address.png)

Changed to private IP:

```
bind-address = 10.1.3.x
```

![Updated Bind](images/changed-MySQL bind-address.png)

---

# 🔗 Connectivity Testing

Connectivity between instances was verified using:

### Ping

```
ping <private-ip>
```

### Telnet

```
telnet 10.1.2.x 8080
telnet 10.1.3.x 3306
```

---

# 📝 Conclusion

This project demonstrates a **secure and scalable 3-Tier AWS Architecture** using:

- Custom VPC
- Public & Private Subnets
- NAT Gateway
- EC2 instances
- Nginx (Web Layer)
- Tomcat (Application Layer)
- MySQL (Database Layer)

This setup follows **AWS cloud architecture best practices for security and scalability.**

---
